f1-door-reach.title: How far does the door actually reach today, and does the epic's stated repro still hold?
f1-door-reach.imperative: Resolve from the code and the live door: count the surviving CLI-fallback clauses and <engine> tokens, list the door's registered tools against the engine's verbs, and establish whether a role agent can reach its OWN spine through the door. Record the code evidence.
f1-door-reach.finding: MEASURED 2026-08-16 @600de02: 15 CLI-fallback clauses across 11 files (charter, workbench SKILL+checklist-engine, explorer SKILL+spine tmpl x2, interrogator SKILL, write-a-skill survey+gated-engine tmpls, commander spine tmpl x3 + commander-core, admiral spine tmpl x2); 11 <engine> tokens across 7 files incl. scripts/init_work_area.py. Door registers 11 tools covering every engine verb EXCEPT there is no verb to BIND an existing spine: spine_open only MINTS a new worktree+branch+spine. Live proof this run: spine_status REFUSED with 'no spine is bound to this door' in the Admiral's own session, so the Admiral drove its own spine on the CLI fallback. specs/ holds only implementer.spine.toml and reviewer.spine.toml; neither carries door vocabulary. Epic repro HOLDS and extends: the unreachable-own-spine defect (#559 collision 2) is not confined to dispatched subagents -- it hits the top-tier orchestrator in its own process.

q1-scope.title: What is in this epic's scope, and how does it wave up?
q1-scope.imperative: Take to the human: the member set (#559, #565, #432, #541, #442, #535), which slurp candidates come in, and the proposed wave shape. Scope branches every later question, so resolve it first and alone.
q1-scope.finding: HUMAN ANSWER 2026-08-16: two waves, seven lanes. W1 (parallel, unblocks): A=#559 per-dispatch spine identity + the bind-own-spine gap + #613's save()-atomicity half; B=#432 ExternalBackend spine-terminal verification; C=#442 rail/refusal readability paired with #595; G=#574 one-verb mechanical closeout + #552 lease-release-on-archive. CHECKPOINT. W2 (the subtraction wave): D=doctrine sweep (15 clauses, 11 <engine> tokens) + #565 workbench sunset + regrowth guard + doc co-travelers #561/#596/#526; E=#541 door rejections into episode friction; F=#535 reveal spec through spine. All four slurp groups accepted.

q2-checkpoints.title: Stop-and-present at every wave boundary, or cleared to run ahead?
q2-checkpoints.imperative: Take to the human: the checkpoint protocol and what reaches them at a checkpoint.
q2-checkpoints.finding: HUMAN ANSWER: stop-and-present at each wave boundary. Two checkpoints: post-W1, and closeout acceptance. Plain-English summary plus decision asks; evidence on demand.

q3-decision-classes.title: Which decision classes are delegated to the Admiral, and which are surfaced?
q3-decision-classes.imperative: Take to the human. Note the project overlay's standing rule: pushes, PRs and merges to main require explicit human approval unless pre-approved for the specified work. Settle the pre-clearance/fallback row for each delegated class, since the harness permission classifier can veto regardless (#145, #408).
q3-decision-classes.finding: HUMAN ANSWER: DELEGATED = merge to main (pre-approved for epic #567 specifically, satisfying the overlay's 'unless pre-approved for the specified work' clause) and fix-now triage. SURFACED = architecture/structural change. ISSUE FILING IS NOT DELEGATED AND NOT MERELY SURFACED -- the human ruled it HELD: 'we've been ballooning out tracking. let's hold on to them until the end then see if we can pair them with open issues, anything else we can file under episodes.' Operationally: no lane files any issue during the run; triage candidates accumulate under .agent-work/epic-567-door/triage-candidates/; at closeout each is paired against an OPEN issue as a comment where one fits, and whatever does not pair is recorded as an episode rather than minted as a new issue. Admiral's stated reading, open to correction: closing the epic's OWN member issues on verified-merged remains delegated as the tail of the merge class.

q4-budget.title: Wave width and model tier per lane?
q4-budget.imperative: Take to the human: how many Commanders run concurrently, at what model tier, and how the usage-limit window sizes the waves.
q4-budget.finding: HUMAN ANSWER: all four W1 lanes concurrent. Opus Commander on lane A (#559, design-heavy, load-bearing interface); Sonnet Commanders on B, C, G. Usage window is a wave-sizing input: defer a dispatch past a near reset rather than launching into it.

q5-expiry.title: When does this contract expire?
q5-expiry.imperative: Take to the human: a time or an event that forces a contract-refresh decision before further dispatch.
q5-expiry.finding: HUMAN ANSWER: expires at the W1 checkpoint. Crossing into W2 forces a contract refresh.

consolidation.summary: Latitude contract for epic-567-door settled and signed by Tommy 2026-08-16. Two waves, seven lanes; W1 = A(#559+bind-own-spine+#613 atomicity, Opus), B(#432), C(#442+#595), G(#574+#552) all concurrent on Sonnet except A; stop-and-present at each wave boundary; merge-to-main and fix-now triage delegated, architecture surfaced, issue FILING held to closeout with triage candidates staged under triage-candidates/ and dispositioned by pairing onto open issues or recording as episodes; contract expires at the W1 checkpoint. Nine pre-rulings recorded, incl. self-hosting engine-edit safety, fresh-process validation of engine/hook changes, human-only design convergence on lane A, and every-lane-deletes. Contract at .agent-work/epic-567-door/LATITUDE_CONTRACT.md; record at INTERROGATION_RECORD.json (verifier exit 0).
